title: One call, and the town split in two.
subtitle: Salih is sent to Thamud
then: Allah sent Salih to Thamud, {idea}one of their own{/idea}, calling them to worship Allah alone. Mujahid said they became two parties: {trap}believers and disbelievers{/trap}, quarreling with each other. Ibn Kathir links it to the arrogant leaders mocking the weak who believed.
now: You start praying at work, or stop joining the gossip at lunch. Suddenly there are two groups at the table. {idea}You did not make the split. You made the choice visible.{/idea} Stay kind with both sides.
old: If doing right causes friction, I must be doing something wrong.
new: A clear call to good will sometimes show where people already stand.
try: Keep one good practice today even if it makes you stand out, and stay gentle about it.

title: Why rush toward harm instead of good?
subtitle: Salih asks his people to seek forgiveness
then: Ibn Kathir explains Salih's question: {trap}why are you praying for the punishment to come{/trap}, and not asking Allah for His mercy? He urged them to {reward}seek forgiveness so they might receive mercy.{/reward}
now: Your doctor warns about your blood pressure and you joke: something has to get me eventually. {trap}Daring the warning feels brave.{/trap} The wiser move is quieter: ask for help and change course while the door is open.
old: If the warning is real, let it happen and we will see.
new: When I am warned, the smart response is to seek forgiveness, not to dare the consequence.
try: Say astaghfirullah three times today, thinking of one specific thing.

title: They blamed him for their bad luck.
subtitle: Calling the messenger a bad omen

key.label: Where the bad luck comes from

then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}whenever anything bad happened to them, they said it was because of Salih and his companions.{/trap} Salih answered that their fate was with Allah. Qatadah explained: {idea}you are being tested to see whether you will obey or disobey.{/idea}
now: The car breaks down the week your new colleague starts. The house feels unlucky since your sister-in-law moved in. {trap}It is easy to make a person the reason.{/trap} The question is how you respond to the test.
old: When things go wrong, someone must be bringing bad luck.
new: Hard times are tests from Allah, not proof that someone is cursed.
try: Catch one moment today when you blame a person for bad luck. Replace it with a dua.

title: Nine men spread corruption and never set things right.
subtitle: The ringleaders of Thamud
then: Ibn Kathir says these nine {trap}forced their opinions on the people because they were the leaders.{/trap} Ibn Abbas said they instigated the killing of the she-camel. Ata said {trap}they used to break silver coins{/trap}, and Sa'id bin Al-Musayyib called cutting coins part of spreading corruption.
now: Shaving a few minutes off timesheets. Short-changing a customer by a coin. Pushing your opinion on the whole family because you are the eldest. {trap}Corruption often starts small and from the top.{/trap}
old: Corruption is what powerful people do on the news.
new: Corruption includes the small cheats and the pressure I put on people below me.
try: Fix one small unfairness you have been letting slide, even if no one would notice.

title: They swore by Allah to commit a crime.
subtitle: The night plot against Salih
then: Ibn Kathir explains they plotted to kill Salih and his family at night, then tell his relatives {trap}they knew nothing, and that they were telling the truth because none of them had seen anything.{/trap} They sealed it with an oath by Allah.
now: "I never said that" when you typed it. "I did not take it" when you let someone else do it. {trap}Wording a lie to sound true still makes it a lie.{/trap} Allah knows what you planned.
old: If my words are technically true, I am not lying.
new: A clever wording does not hide the truth of what I did from Allah.
try: Notice one time today you are tempted to give a technically true answer. Give the honest one.

title: They planned, and Allah planned.
subtitle: The plot they could not see coming
then: Ibn Abi Hatim reports they waited in a cave near Salih's place of prayer to kill him. {idea}A rock came down from the mountain and covered the cave's mouth{/idea} with them inside. {reward}Allah saved Salih and those with him.{/reward}
now: Someone at work is quietly building a case against you. Your ex is spreading stories. It keeps you up at night. {idea}Their plan is not the last plan.{/idea} Do what is right, and trust the One who sees everything.
old: If people are plotting against me, I have to out-plot them.
new: Allah has a plan above every plan, and they do not see it coming.
try: Hand one worry about someone's scheming to Allah in dua tonight, then sleep.

title: Look how their plotting ended.
subtitle: The outcome of the plan against Salih
then: Mujahid said {trap}before they could reach Salih, they and their people were all destroyed.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says Allah punished some of them in one place and some in another. The verse asks the listener to look at how it ended.
now: You have watched someone build their success on lies and lose it all. {idea}The verse asks you to look, not to gloat.{/idea} Ask where your own plans are headed.
old: Stories of ruined people are about someone else.
new: Every ending I see is a mirror for checking where my own plans lead.
try: Look at one plan you are working on. Ask how it ends if you keep going this way.

title: Empty houses that still speak.
subtitle: The ruins of Thamud as a sign
then: Their houses were left {trap}in utter ruin, deserted, because they did wrong.{/trap} The verse says this is {idea}a sign for people who know.{/idea} The listeners in Makkah knew the old ruins of Thamud.
now: You walk past a shop that closed, a once-grand house now empty. {idea}Every abandoned place says: nothing here is permanent.{/idea} People who know take the lesson home with them.
new: Empty places remind me that only what I do for Allah lasts.
try: The next empty or abandoned building you pass, say a short dua for a good ending.

title: Those who believed and were mindful were saved.
subtitle: The rescue inside the story
then: After the ruin, the verse turns: {reward}Allah saved those who believed and had taqwa.{/reward} Ibn Kathir notes the believers had been called a bad omen and were the weaker party. They were the ones who came through.
now: You feel outnumbered: the only one in your office who prays, the one parent who sets screen limits. {reward}Being few is not the same as being lost.{/reward} Faith and mindfulness are what carry you through.
old: If I am in the minority, I am on the losing side.
new: Safety comes from faith and mindfulness of Allah, not from numbers.
try: Thank Allah today for one person who shares your faith and helps you keep it.

title: Doing wrong openly, with eyes wide open.
subtitle: Lut confronts his people
then: Lut warned his people of Allah's punishment. Ibn Kathir explains {trap}while you see{/trap} as {trap}while you see one another, practicing every kind of evil in your meetings.{/trap} They knew what they were doing, and did it openly.
now: The group chat where everyone shares what should not be shared. The office joke no one stops. {trap}When wrong becomes normal in the room, it gets harder to see.{/trap} Notice where you have stopped noticing.
old: If everyone around me does it openly, it cannot be that bad.
new: Doing wrong openly, with full knowledge, is a sign the heart has gone numb.
try: Leave or quietly change one gathering, chat or habit where wrong has become normal.

title: Desire leading where knowledge said no.
subtitle: Lut calls his people ignorant
then: Lut said they were a people who behave senselessly. Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}you do not know anything of what is natural or what is prescribed by Allah.{/trap} He links it to their leaving what Allah had created for them.
now: Late at night, you know what you should close, delete, or walk away from. {trap}Desire talks louder than what you know.{/trap} The verse calls that ignorance, even when you know better.
old: My desires are just part of me, so following them is natural.
new: Letting desire overrule what Allah taught me is a kind of ignorance.
try: Next time a desire pushes against what you know is right, wait five minutes before acting.

title: Their only answer: throw out the clean ones.
subtitle: Purity treated as a crime
then: They gave no other answer. Ibn Kathir explains their thinking: {trap}these people feel embarrassed by your deeds and do not approve, so expel them.{/trap} Lut's family was accused of one thing: {idea}wanting to stay pure.{/idea}
now: Your friends tease you for not drinking at the party, for leaving early, for not joining the gossip. "You think you are better than us." {idea}Sometimes your example is the whole argument.{/idea}
old: If people push me out for my standards, I must be doing something wrong.
new: Being pushed away for staying clean can be a sign I am holding on to something good.
try: Keep one standard today that others tease you for, and smile when they do.

title: Saved, except the one who helped the wrong.
subtitle: Lut's wife remained behind
then: Ibn Kathir says Lut's wife was destroyed with her people {trap}because she was a helper to what they did and approved of their evil deeds.{/trap} She told them about Lut's guests. Being married to a prophet did not save her.
now: You did not write the cruel post, you just liked it. You did not cheat, you just told him where the answers were. {trap}Helping and approving are their own deeds.{/trap} And who you are close to will not carry you.
old: If I did not commit the wrong myself, I am not involved.
new: Helping or approving of wrong counts, and being close to good people will not save me alone.
try: Undo one small way you have been helping or cheering on something wrong.

title: They were warned, and still went ahead.
subtitle: The end of Lut's people
then: Ibn Kathir says the rain was stones, one after another. It fell on {trap}those against whom proof was established and whom the warning reached{/trap}, yet they denied the Messenger and resolved to drive him out.
now: You have heard the reminder at Jumuah, read the verse, been told kindly by a friend. {idea}Hearing the warning is a mercy.{/idea} It is still not too late to act on it today.
old: I have heard all the warnings before, so they do not apply to me anymore.
new: Every warning I have heard is a mercy and a responsibility while I still have time.
try: Think of one reminder you keep hearing and ignoring. Take one small step on it today.
